Name: Resonance
Author: pneuma163
Description:
[size=3]Originally inspired by the flute block puzzle in Island Southeast with the mermaid, Resonance adds a Resonant Flute and numerous short tunes that you can play to affect the world and your interactions with it.[/size]

[size=6][u][b]How to install:[/b][/u][/size]

[list=1]
[*][size=3][url=https://smapi.io]Install the latest version of SMAPI[/url].[/size]
[*][size=3]Download this mod and unzip it into [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/Mods[/font].[/size]
[*][size=3]Run the game using SMAPI.[/size]
[/list][size=3]If you need additional help installing the mod, the [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Player_Guide/Getting_Started]Stardew Valley wiki[/url]﻿ has more detailed instructions.
To uninstall the mod, delete this mod's folder from your Mods folder. If you left anything in the resonant receptacle, retrieve that first and then save your game before uninstalling or the items may be lost.
[/size]
[size=3]Note: Resonance can be installed (or removed) at any time.[/size]

[size=6][b][u]What is a song?[/u][/b][/size]

[size=3]In the context of Resonance, a song is like a bit of magic that affects the world around you somehow. See song descriptions to find out what they do. A song usually consists of a sequence of notes and one or more items. If it's helpful, think of these as musical components and material components, respectively.[/size]

[b][u][size=6]How do I get a Resonant Flute?[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]There will be an in game quest that you receive as you play that will offer a bit of lore and guidance. Note that if you already have a flute in your inventory, you cannot get a second.[/size]

[size=4][b]How, specifically, do I get the flute?[/b][/size]

[size=3]Click the spoiler:[/size]

[spoiler]At any time, take a piece of hardwood with you into the frozen floors of the mines (40-79) and use it like a tool (left click while holding it) on one of the ice crystals in the mines.[/spoiler]

[b][u][size=6]How do I play the flute? How do I navigate the Instrument Menu?[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]Press right click (or whatever you have bound to the "check/do action" control) while holding the Resonant Flute and a menu will appear. This is called the Instrument Menu. On the left you will see songs that you can play. Flip pages by pressing left/right. On the right you will see the note that the flute is currently set to. Click to play that note. Change the note by pressing up/down or by scrolling on a mouse.

Additionally, you can play notes using the keybinds set in the config.json (a file created when you launch the game with the mod installed). You can change these by editing the config file or by using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url]. Pressing 1 through = on a keyboard plays the flute at pitches C4 through B4. Hold left shift to raise the pitch an octave. Play C6 by holding left shift, Q, and pressing 1. Controller users do not currently have default keybinds, so I recommend using GMCM to set those if you want to play the instrument that way. Note that these keybinds only apply when the menu is open.

Finally, if you play a song but do not have the material components nearby (more on that below), a description of the song's effect will appear for a few seconds.[/size]

[b][u][size=6]How do I play a song?[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]If you haven't, read the answer above to "How do I play the flute? How do I navigate the menu?" first.

A song usually consists of a sequence of notes and one or more items. If it's helpful, think of these as musical components and material components, respectively.

You can either drop the items on the ground or place them into a "resonant receptacle" that you have placed on the ground. Resonant magic requires in-world interactions, so it does not look at the player's inventory. If you use the resonant receptacle, it can be anywhere in the location where you are currently, but if you drop items on the ground then they can be at most a few tiles away (this distance can be configured).

If you drop items on the ground and quickly open the Instrument Menu, you will not pick up those items, no matter how strong your magnet is. Since that requires timing, you may instead place a resonant receptacle on the ground by left clicking (the "use tool" control) with the flute somewhere on the ground and a receptacle will appear. Now, still holding the flute, you can right click on the receptacle and it will open a small inventory like a chest that can hold 3 stacks of items. You can place material components inside.

Finally, now that you have the material components available, open the Instrument Menu and play the song you want! Tempo does not matter, only pitch. A song will not be effective if its conditions are not met, though, so read its description or risk losing your materials! (You can configure whether a failed song will cause your materials to be lost.) If a song requires proximity to whatever it affects, that distance is measured from the materials, not from the player.

(Also, [i]usually[/i] a song requires items, but I am here spreading rumors about the existence of secret songs that only need the correct notes.)[/size]

[b][u][size=6]What do the songs do?[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]Some songs warp you around the world. There are songs for healing and for restoring stamina. One song can guarantee you a fishing treasure chest. One song can increase your friendship with people you're hanging out with. Another calls your horse to you. You can see more in the menu within the mod itself, but also:[/size]

[b][u][size=6]Future of the mod[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]More songs! Or more specifically, more ways you can interact with the world. I wanted this mod to offer new ways to affect the player and the world using a new mechanic that still feels close to what we already see in the game (like the mermaid's song), so expect future updates to include expansions on that idea. Related to this, current songs may change or even be removed.[/size]

[b][u][size=6]Compatibility[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]Built for Stardew 1.6.15+

Tested on Linux, should work just as well on Mac and Windows.

Tested somewhat in multiplayer and should work quite well, including the ability to hear another player and even contribute music (but not materials) to a player who is close by. Whoever plays the final note gets credit for the song. Not tested on splitscreen, but it is designed to work there as well, so please let me know if you encounter bugs or strange behavior.

Android is untested and I have no idea if it will work. If it does, I'd be interested to hear, but I cannot fix bugs on Android if they appear.[/size]

[b][u][size=6]Can I add more songs that do things?[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]You can add songs using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1915]Content Patcher[/url]. Here is an example content.json:[/size]

[code]{
"Format": "2.8.0",
"Changes": [
{
"LogName": "pneuma163's Resonance Pack Demo",
"Action": "EditData",
"Target": "pneuma163.Resonance/SongData",
"Entries": {
"{{ModId}}_AddSpeed": { //must start with your mod's unique id: e.g. {{ModId}}_exampletext
"Id": "{{ModId}}_AddSpeed", //must match the line above
"DisplayName": "Burst of Speed", //the name of the song that the player sees
"Description": "Briefly increase your speed", //a description of the song
"Notes": "1200, 1400, 1500", //comma-separated integers from 0 to 2400, multiples of 100. 0 is C4 (middle C) and 2400 is C6 two octaves higher. There must be from 3 to 8 (inclusive).
"MaterialComponents": "(O)390 3 color_red 1", //an item's qualified ID or a context tag followed by a quantity, up to three stacks may be listed (i.e. this is a valid entry with two: a stack of 3 stone and a stack of 1 red item)
"Condition": "TRUE", //optional: a game state query, defaults to true. If this is false, the trigger actions in EffectActions do not happen and the song fails (the player may lose the materials)
"EffectDelay": 750, //optional: how long after the song to do the effects (0 to 2000 ms, default is 750)
"AudioEffect": "getNewSpecialItem", //optional: an audio cue to play after the song, defaults to silence
"EffectActions": ["AddBuff 22 1000"], //optional: (but you probably want it) a list of trigger actions that are triggered after the song
"RecipeMenuVisibility": "Visible" //optional: whether the song appears in the menu. Default is Visible. Currently supported values: Visible, Hidden
}
}
}
]
}[/code]

[b][u][size=6]Translations[/size][/u][/b]

[size=3]You must read and agree to the [url=https://next.nexusmods.com/profile/pneuma163]translation guidelines and restrictions[/url] found on my profile. Any translation or mod found to be in violation of those restrictions will be reported for abuse.

[/size][size=6][b][u]Console commands[/u][/b][/size][size=3]

[size=3]Here are some console commands that you may find useful:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=3][font=Courier New]reson.pflute <int>[/font] - Play the flute at the given pitch[/size]
[*][size=3][font=Courier New]reson.song <notesString>[/font] - Plays the given notes in sequence, half a second at a time, e.g. reson.song "1200, 1400, 1500"[/size]
[*][size=3][font=Courier New]reson.tag[/font] - Prints items with the given tag[/size]
[*][size=3][font=Courier New]reson.debug <NameOfNPC>[/font] - Turn on debug mode[/size]
[/list]
